title: Game Core W0 protocol fixture case file
description: Canonical shape of every file under Data/cases. The companion result document shape is described in x-result-document, and the executable semantics of each kind in x-kinds.

caseId.description: Stable identifier, unique across all case files.

requirementIds.description: Normative requirement anchors in docs/game-core/00-core-protocols.md that this case exercises.

testIds.description: Acceptance suite anchors in docs/game-core/08-validation-and-performance.md; the first entry is the case's primary suite in the result document.

outcome.description: What the case claims about the input: 'valid' means the input satisfies the protocol, 'invalid' means the oracle must refuse it.

code.description: Required rejection code when outcome is 'invalid'. It must be one of the required diagnostic code literals from 00 s9 or one of the oracle's detector codes listed in x-kinds.

cases.caseId: case identifier from the case file
cases.testId: primary TEST-nnn suite of the case
cases.detail: what was expected and what the oracle observed

outcomes.Pass: the oracle agreed with the case's stated expectation
outcomes.Fail: the oracle disagreed with the case's stated expectation, including a missing or different rejection code
outcomes.NotRun: the case was not executed on this host
outcomes.Blocked: the case could not be evaluated because its data is malformed or its probe name is unknown; a delivered run must contain neither NotRun nor Blocked

idCanonicalBytes.asserts: the canonical byte sequence of a stable id is the high word then the low word, each big-endian; refusal code CanonicalBytesMismatch or HexRoundTripMismatch

parameters.expectedCanonicalOrder: the same ids in canonical order
parameters.permutations: optional array of insertion orders given as index arrays; when omitted, every insertion order of up to six ids is generated

stableIdOrder.asserts: numeric and canonical-byte sorting agree and are independent of insertion order; refusal codes PermutationOrderMismatch, ByteOrderMismatch, ComparisonPathsDisagree

parameters.requiredActivationEpoch: optional unsigned 64-bit; 0 means no execution authority required

handleValidation.asserts: dereference validation order world, slot presence, generation, liveness, category, activation epoch; refusal codes are WrongWorld, MissingSlot, StaleGeneration, NotLive, WrongCategory, StaleActivationEpoch

worldCollision.asserts: handles collide only for the same world incarnation, slot and generation, and a restored world rejects the previous incarnation's handle; refusal codes CollisionMismatch, IncarnationNotSeparated

parameters.counter: CompositionRevision | AssemblyEpoch | ActivationEpoch | LogicalStepId | InstallationGeneration | DefinitionRevision | EventSequence
parameters.current: unsigned 64-bit, as a JSON number or a decimal string

counterAdvance.asserts: the counter advances by exactly one, or refuses at its maximum without wrapping; refusal code OverflowRejected or WrappedInsteadOfRejected

publicationAdvance.asserts: a publication moves revision and epoch but never the step, NoChange moves nothing, a committed step moves only the step, and an exhausted revision refuses; refusal codes OverflowRejected, PublicationInvariantViolated, StepChangedOnPublication, NoChangeMovedCounters, CompositionMovedOnStep

parameters.knownFeatures: optional array of hex feature ids
parameters.requiredFeatures: optional array of hex feature ids

versionSupport.asserts: protocol version interpretation: majors are incompatible, minors must fall inside the declared window, unknown required features reject, and a mismatch is never accepted silently; refusal code UnsupportedVersion or SilentFallback

parameters.assemblyName: simple assembly name to inspect; the tokens {oracleAssembly} and {kernelAssembly} are substituted by the runner with the assembly actually loaded in the test process
parameters.forbiddenNamespacePrefixes: optional array of namespace prefixes that must not appear in exported types
parameters.forbiddenAssemblyNames: optional array of referenced assembly names that must not appear
parameters.requiredReferences: optional array of referenced assembly names that must appear; the same two tokens are substituted here

assemblyIndependence.asserts: the kernel-only boundary: the oracle and the kernel contract assembly it compiles against reference neither an engine nor a gameplay assembly; refusal codes GameplayOrEngineDependency, MissingSeamReference, ForbiddenNamespace, AssemblyNotLoadable

parameters.candidates: array of { text, accepted } objects (a bare string or null is read as { text, accepted: true|false })

idHexParsing.asserts: there is exactly one accepted hexadecimal form: 32 lowercase characters, no whitespace, sign or prefix; the oracle parser and the seam parser agree on every candidate, an accepted candidate round-trips to identical text, and non-canonical near misses are refused; refusal codes ParserDisagreement, ParserExpectationMismatch, NonCanonicalFormAccepted, SeamRejectedCanonicalHex, SeamHexFormDiffers, HexRoundTripMismatch

parameters.requiredLiterals: the code literals the implementation must expose

diagnosticCodeText.asserts: every enum value maps to a unique literal equal to its name, text parsing round-trips to the same value, every declared required literal is present, and an unknown literal is refused; refusal codes DuplicateLiteral, LiteralRoundTripFailed, LiteralDiffersFromName, RequiredLiteralMissing, UnknownLiteralAccepted

parameters.schemaId: 32-character hex schema id carried in the header
parameters.schemaVersion: unsigned schema version carried in the header
parameters.probe: checksumRoundTrip | checksumTamper | fieldTypeRoundTrip | canonicalNaN | unknownRequiredFeature | knownRequiredFeature | writerFieldIdZero | writerFieldIdTooLarge | writerListHeaderOverLimit | writerListBytesOverLimit | readerBoolByte | readerFieldIdOutOfRange | readerListCountExceeded | readerListTooLarge | readerTruncatedField
parameters.declaredCount: count declared by a hand-assembled list header (readerListCountExceeded)
parameters.declaredBytes: byte length declared by a hand-assembled list header (readerListTooLarge)

envelopeCodec.asserts: the trailing FNV-1a checksum verifies a written document and detects one flipped covered byte; every wire type round-trips bit-exactly, including signed integers and IEEE-754 floats; both NaN payloads become the single canonical quiet NaN; an unknown required feature rejects before the body is used; reserved or out-of-range field ids are refused on both sides; list count and byte length are bounded on both sides; a bool byte other than 0 or 1 and a truncated field record are refused
envelopeCodec.independence-note: unlike the identity, counter and version oracles, these probes deliberately drive the seam's own envelope codec: the envelope is a codec whose declared read/write rules are what the fixtures pin down, and byte-level documents the writer would refuse are hand-assembled so the reader's limit checks are exercisable

x-source-of-truth: docs/game-core/00-core-protocols.md is the only normative source; a case's expected outcome is derived from the requirement it names, never from the reference seam implementation.

The oracle re-implements canonical byte order, comparison, handle validation, counter arithmetic and version interpretation instead of calling the seam, so the two can disagree and a seam defect is observable.
A case's expected rejection code must be a required diagnostic literal from 00 s9 or a detector code documented in x-kinds; a typo fails the suite rather than passing silently.
Fixture data is never edited to make a failing oracle pass; a mismatch means either the fixture or the implementation is wrong and must be corrected at the normative source.

Envelope probes are the one kind that intentionally exercises the seam codec rather than an independent re-implementation; every other kind re-derives the semantics from 00 so a seam defect is observable as a disagreement.
